messages.content: "Can you help me plan a day out in Seattle, WA for my group of 10 friends? We are food lovers and would like to try some Seafood and Italian cuisine for lunch. Later in the evening, we are interested in attending a Concert or a Sports event. Could you find suitable restaurants and events for us?"

function.name: restaurant_find_group
function.description: Find restaurants suitable for groups based on specified criteria such as location and cuisine. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Seattle, WA

cuisine.description: Preferred cuisine at the restaurant. Default is all if not specified.

group_size.description: Size of the group that the restaurant should accommodate.

function.name: events_find_event
function.description: Find events suitable for groups based on specified criteria such as location and event type. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Seattle, WA

event_type.description: Type of event. Default is all if not specified.

group_size.description: Size of the group that the event should accommodate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants restaurants and events for a group of 10 in Seattle, WA. They want seafood and Italian for lunch, and later a concert or sports event. We need to call both functions. The user didn't specify a group size for the restaurant search, but they said group of 10. So we can use group_size=10. For the restaurant search, we need location and group_size. We can also provide cuisine preferences: "Seafood" and "Italian". The function expects cuisine?: "Seafood" | "Italian" | "Chinese"[]. That means we can pass an array of strings. So we can pass ["Seafood", "Italian"]. For events, we need location and group_size. We can also provide event_type: "Concert" | "Sports" | "Exhibition" | "Festival"[]. So we can pass ["Concert", "Sports"].

We should call the restaurant_find_group function first with location="Seattle, WA", group_size=10, cuisine=["Seafood", "Italian"]. Then call events_find_event with location="Seattle, WA", group_size=10, event_type=["Concert", "Sports"].

We should not mention the function name or arguments in the response. We just call the function.
